Let's denote the vectors of the given sets as 
${{u}_{1},{u}_{2}},$
${{v}_{1},{v}_{2}},$ and 
${{w}_{1},{w}_{2}}$, respectively. 

The sets $U,V,$ and $W$ are orthonormal if the following conditions on each set hold:

- ${u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2}=0\,\text{and}\,{\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}=1 \\ {u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}$

- ${v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{2}=0\,\text{and}\,{\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}=1 \\ {v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}$

- ${w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2}=0\,\text{and}\,{\begin{aligned}{w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{1}=1 \\ {w}_{2}\cdot {w}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}$

With that in mind, let's examine our sets in turn.

- For the set $U,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ -\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{3}{10}-\frac{3}{10}=0 & ✓ \\ {u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{9}{10}+\frac{1}{10}=1 & ✓ \\ {u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ -\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ -\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{10}+\frac{9}{10}=1 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, the set $U$ is orthonormal.

- For the set $V,$ notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=-1-1=-2\ne 0 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

So, $V$ is not an orthonormal set.

- For the set $W,$ notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}{w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=-\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}=-\frac{3}{\sqrt{5}}\ne 0 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

So, $W$ is not an orthonormal set.

Therefore, we conclude that the correct answer is "$U$ only".
